answer: Agents can earn reputation only through repeated, escrow-backed trades with counterparties that already have history; each trade locks a deposit, and a dispute lets the counterparty slash it for fraud. One fabricated identity gains little because it cannot cheaply create trusted counterparties: cycling trades among its own accounts yields no independent history. The attacker must recruit established agents or risk real capital on deposits, while genuine newcomers can build standing gradually, even if their first walnut shipment reaches a harbor after they wander far from home.
